title: Prime-length necklaces
notes: The movable-card method already exists: use the supplied eight- and 32-card sheets, cut into rectangles before use if desired, and group the cards physically; no handwritten reproduction of the catalog is required. Keep one adult at each table, with partners sharing and checking rotation families. For another visit, K-1 can compare four-bead periods (P3-4), then the five-/six-bead examples (P5-6). Grades 2-3 can sort the supplied five-bead cards cooperatively (P4) and justify the count (P5-6). Grades 4-5 can return to the prime-period theorem and general color count (P5-6), using the saved families as examples. Keep rings face up.
